intended: All four runs are titanium at Kestrel Works on the night shift inside one quarter, so one retooling covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter" and that "every logged run was cut on one of those machines", so the refit reached all four runs. A change of insert grade moves cycle time by itself, and each run is compared against the same run last quarter, when the older grade was still fitted, rather than against a run on the same inserts over the same period. The 4 to 7 minute reductions cannot be separated from the retooling.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A faster insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who kept up the home exercises, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake let those exercises lapse. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the averages describe three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders stay stiff and painful are the ones who let the exercises go, so the quarter held out of the average is where the flat and negative results sit and the reported degrees are an average over the patients who were already doing well. All four intakes are rotator cuff cases on the Marbeck ward in one spring and each leaves out the same quarter, so no case in the register covers the patients the others miss.
reported: The abduction averages "cover the patients who kept up the home exercises" while "a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse", so the 14/11/16/9 degree gains come only from the adherent three-quarters. Adherers are systematically the patients with less pain and better function, so the selected subset, not the protocol, can produce the gain.

reported: The averages "cover the patients who kept up the home exercises" while "a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse" - so the reported abduction gains are a per-protocol figure computed on the compliant three quarters, and the excluded quarter is precisely the group least likely to have improved. The steroid confound is genuinely blocked (intakes were barred from injections), but the selective averaging is not.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the purchase counts over the sessions that reached the new page, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout. The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases across the segment, so the population is every session in the segment and the counts describe three quarters of it. Sessions that break off before checkout are the ones that buy nothing, and a checkout page changes how many sessions get that far, so a rise measured over the sessions that arrived is consistent with purchases across the whole segment holding flat. All four segments are desktop sessions from Canada via search inside March and the same quarter drops out of each, so no case in the log supplies what the others leave out.
reported: The purchase counts "cover the sessions that reached the new page" while "a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout", so the 6/4/7/5 percent gains are computed on the surviving three-quarters that got as far as the new checkout page, not on all sessions. That is a narrower population than the claim about purchases overall, and a page that lifts the rate among reachers can leave total purchases flat.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the infection rates over the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol. The claim is about ward infection rates, which is a claim about everyone the ward admitted, so a quarter of that population sits outside the numbers entirely. The patients whose care runs outside the ward's routine for a spell are the ones taken to theatre, to intensive care or to another unit, and those are the patients who pick up infections, so the reported drop is measured over the patients who ran the straightforward course. The four entries span four hospitals, four ward types, four quarters and four auditors, and the spells-outside clause applies at each ward, so every case is missing the same quarter of its own population.
reported: The reported rates cover a narrower population than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." A quarter of each ward's patients are dropped, so the 6-11 percent falls describe a selected fully-compliant subgroup rather than the ward's infection rate.
